answer: In an agent economy, a mirror of on-chain stake history lets peers verify continuous participation across epochs. Agents must maintain a minimum locked balance that grows with network activity; a sybil cluster would need to fund many such locks simultaneously. The ripple of any sudden mass creation appears as anomalous stake concentration in the canyon of low-activity addresses, raising the attacker cost because each fake identity requires independent capital that cannot be recycled without leaving detectable traces.
